ci_run: 45784180164 (3/3 PASS; not evidence of production safety)

findings.summary: PCB durable runner mints receipt lineage '{task_id}:effect:N' while #180 changed the L3 intent identity to canonical 'EF-<sha256>'. core/durable_loop.py:465 rejects every receipt.
findings.reproduction: Run main() with stubbed run_kit, --max-steps 1 -> state BLOCKED: 'execution receipt lineage does not match persisted intent'. Test: tests/test_stack_audit_remediation.py::test_pcb_eda_receipt_lineage_matches_canonical_intent (fails on 140c032).
findings.impact: Every receipt-governed pcb.eda@1 / discover_evidence step BLOCKs; runner non-functional. Fail-closed (no unsafe PASS), but availability regression undetected by CI because no test drives main().

findings.summary: Roll-forward trusts absolute 'tmp'/'dest' paths from journal.v2.json; body_digest is unkeyed SHA-256. No containment check.
findings.reproduction: Plant .staging/batch-x/journal.v2.json with dest=<outside store> and recomputed digest; recover_pending() writes attacker bytes outside the store. Tests: test_rollforward_quarantines_dest_outside_store, test_rollforward_quarantines_tmp_outside_batch, test_commit_batch_rejects_escaping_destination.
findings.impact: Write access to .aios/.staging escalates to arbitrary file overwrite with the AIOS process's privileges.

findings.summary: recovery_binding is an unkeyed SHA-256 integrity hash stored next to the data it covers. It detects accidental corruption only; it is not authenticated integrity.
findings.reproduction: artifacts/stack-audit-177-180/wal_attack_poc.py: crash after RECEIPT_VALIDATED, rewrite validated_state_patch, recompute binding -> reconcile_in_flight_attempt applies FORGED patch and reaches PASS.
findings.impact: A WAL/snapshot writer can forge recovered state_patch/verification/action_result. Residual protection = execution_receipt_validator + state_patch_validator re-run at recovery (lines 681-696); for PCB these read artifacts in the same writable output dir (INFERRED: same trust domain).

findings.summary: WAL records carry per-record unkeyed checksum + sequence, no hash chain, no signature, no external high-water mark. Deleting in_flight_attempt (append a recomputed record, or truncate tail to a pre-intent record) is undetectable.
findings.reproduction: wal_attack_poc.py F-04: drop in_flight_attempt after crash -> act() invoked twice for one logical operation.
findings.impact: Duplicate external side effect (replay) - the exact property the WAL intent exists to prevent. L5 effect ledger dedupe is not consulted by run_durable_loop before ACT (INFERRED from code path lines 436-453).

findings.summary: Permit is created inside the job in an empty ephemeral AIOS_REPAIR_AUTHORITY_DIR (runner.temp) and authorized immediately. Contract binds run_id/base_sha, so permit_id is only known at run time; there is no channel for an external signer to attest it before authorize().
findings.reproduction: Code path: persist_permit(signer=None) -> no attestation -> authorize() -> 'permit issuer attestation is missing' -> SystemExit BLOCKED.
findings.impact: ci-autonomous-repair is structurally BLOCKED, not merely missing a secret. Adding a signer secret would not fix it without a permit request/attest lifecycle.

findings.summary: Attestation claims = {type,version,algorithm,key_id,contract_id,permit_id,issuer}. No issued_at/expires_at, nonce, audience, or use counter.
findings.impact: A captured attestation is valid forever for its permit; revocation granularity is per key only.

findings.summary: Trust anchor sourced from repository 'vars', not an environment-protected secret/variable. Who can edit repo variables is a repo-settings fact not visible from source.
findings.reproduction: Not verifiable from code; requires repo settings audit.
findings.impact: Anyone able to edit the variable can substitute their own public key and self-attest.

findings.summary: Separation-of-duties check only inspects env AIOS_AUTHORITY_SIGNING_KEY_FILE; a key file present on disk or passed another way is not detected.
findings.impact: Separation is advisory, not enforced; verifier and signer can co-reside.

findings.summary: Provider receipt signing keys (AIOS_PROVIDER_SIGNING_KEYS) and provider verifier keyring are both loaded in the same apply job.
findings.impact: Provider receipts are self-signed by the job that verifies them; provider authenticity is not independent.

findings.summary: batch_dir is created under .staging without fsync of .staging; only batch_dir is fsynced after journal publish. Under power loss the batch_dir entry may be lost while some dest renames are durable.
findings.reproduction: Not reproducible with process-crash tests; requires power-loss/dm-flakey harness.
findings.impact: Possible silent partial commit after power loss. Process-crash consistency is tested; power-loss durability is NOT proven.

findings.summary: Directory fsync errors (including EIO) are swallowed; WalStateStore._fsync_parent_dir raises. Inconsistent durability contract.
findings.impact: An fsync failure is reported as a successful commit.

findings.summary: Quarantine is cleared by the mere existence of RESOLVED.json; no operator identity, signature, or content check.
findings.impact: BLOCKED state is bypassable by any store writer.

findings.summary: Journal stores absolute paths; relocating/restoring the store elsewhere makes pending batches unrecoverable (now quarantined by F-02 fix rather than written to old path).
Relative imports ('from .effect_authority import x', 'from . import runtime') and dynamic imports (importlib/__import__) were not resolved -> false PASS.
findings.impact: Report-only gate could not have detected the most likely violation form (core modules use relative imports).

findings.summary: If WAL has no state record (file deleted/emptied) load() trusts the snapshot JSON, which is unauthenticated.
findings.impact: WAL deletion downgrades recovery source to plain JSON.

findings.summary: attempt defaults to 1 and run_durable_loop never passes another value; there is no governed retry-attempt path for one logical operation.
findings.impact: Retry of the same logical op is impossible by design; callers must vary logical_operation_id (PCB uses ':step-N').
